name: White-cheeked Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Montane forest of vietnam and southern laos
description: A garrulous, sociable bird, often found in large flocks, both single-species and mixed. Warm brown with a gray crown, a broad black mask, and a luminously white cheek spot, and long white-tipped tail.

name: Blue-headed Racquet-tail
rangeDescription: Southern philippines (balabac, palawan, calamian, and adjacent islands)
description: A medium-sized parrot of lowland forest and edge on Palawan and neighboring islands. The two central tail feathers have extended shafts ending in a racket shape.

name: Speckled Boobook
rangeDescription: Sulawesi, including kabaena, muna, and buton islands (to se)
description: A distinctive medium-sized owl with a rounded head, prominent white eyebrows, dark eyes, a white belly, and a widely spotted gray upperside and crown. Found in forest and edge in the lowlands and foothills, often in pairs.

name: Long-billed Woodcreeper
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to southwestern venezuela, northern bolivia, amazonian brazil, and french guiana
description: This large and unmistakable woodcreeper is widespread across much of Amazonia. It has a long pinkish bill, white throat, and distinct white streaking on the neck and breast.

name: Southern Martin
rangeDescription: Bolivia to uruguay and argentina; winters to north to colombia
description: Large swallow with pointed wings and slightly forked tail. Males are deep iridescent purple; females are also entirely dark, but are brownish below, with faint scaling.

name: Elegant Parrot
rangeDescription: Disjunct in southwestern and south-central australia, including kangaroo island
description: Handsome small parrot of southern Australia. Yellowish-green overall, with yellow underbelly, green back, green head, and thin dark blue patch on folded wing.

name: Nariño Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of southwestern colombia (risaralda) to ecuador (cotopaxi)
description: A standard Scytalopus tapaculo: plain dark gray with browner flanks and rump. Acts like a mouse, scurrying around on or near the ground within montane forest.

name: Hooded Grebe
rangeDescription: Breeds submontane lakes of western santa cruz province, southwestern argentina; winters to río santa cruz estuary and adjacent coast, southeastern argentina
description: A beautiful, small grebe of Patagonia that is rare, local, and declining; breeds on a few interior lakes. Nonbreeding birds range to coastal waters and lowland lakes, where they are most often seen in the company of Silvery Grebes.

name: Apical Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Arid scrub of colombia (west of the eastern andes)
description: Medium-sized, dull flycatcher without many distinguishing features; typical of the genus Myiarchus. This species is restricted to Colombia, where it is found in dry woodland and scrubby habitat below 1700m.

name: Kilimanjaro White-eye
rangeDescription: Northern tanzania (mount kilimanjaro, mount meru, and arusha regions)
description: A small, sharp-billed warbler-like bird, olive-yellow with very broad white spectacles around the eyes. Found in montane forest, forest edge, and lush gardens and scrub, usually in hyperactive flocks.

name: Crimson-backed Flameback
rangeDescription: Sri lanka
description: Large, spectacular woodpecker with crimson upperparts, black-scaled pale underparts, and a crested head. Males have a red crest, females a black crest with fine white markings.

name: Flesh-footed Shearwater
rangeDescription: Southern indian and southwestern pacific oceans; winters to arabian sea and northwestern pacific
description: Entirely the color of dark chocolate with a dark-tipped pink bill. Fairly large; similar in size and shape to Pink-footed Shearwater.

name: Gray Bunting
rangeDescription: Southern kamchatka, sakhalin, kuril islands, and northern japan; winters to ryukyu islands (southern japan)
description: Small songbird of shady undergrowth, especially dwarf bamboo thickets, found in mid-elevation coniferous or deciduous forests during summer and in shady woodlands and parks during winter. Male uniquely slate-gray; both sexes have warm, rufous-brown rump and tail.

name: Brownish-headed Antbird
rangeDescription: Southern peru (cusco, madre de dios, and puno) and far west-central bolivia
description: Dull-plumaged antbird with a restricted range in the Andean foothills. Males are grayish brown with small white wing spots; females are similar, but are paler tan below.

name: Cape Rockjumper
rangeDescription: South africa (western and eastern cape province)
description: A striking, gregarious bird that bounces about on rocky mountain slopes and crags in fynbos habitat. The sexes differ: the male has a dark rufous belly and rump, a black throat, and a white moustache; the female is duller, with a streaked chest.

name: Oriental Pratincole
rangeDescription: Eastern asia; winters india to southeastern asia, philippines, and australasia
description: Twisting and turning on long, angular wings, this relative of the sandpipers and plovers gives a swallowlike impression in flight. Adults are brown overall with an elegant black necklace and pale yellow throat.

name: Green-capped Tanager
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of far southeastern peru (puno)
description: Handsome tanager with a small range in the Andes of western Bolivia and southeastern Peru. It is pale with blue wings and tail, black mask, and buffy crown and vent.

name: Kipengere Seedeater
rangeDescription: Southern tanzania (mount rungwe and udzungwa mountains)
description: A large seedeater with a big, bulging bill. Dark brown above and white below with heavily streaked underparts.

name: Southern Chestnut-breasted Wren
rangeDescription: Tropical and subtropical east slope of andes of peru south and east of the maranon river (amazonas south to puno) and western bolivia (la paz)
description: Found at higher elevations than other members of its genus. Shy and uncommon denizen of forest undergrowth from 1,100–2,000 m.

name: Madagascar Flufftail
rangeDescription: Humid forest of eastern and northwestern madagascar
description: Tiny, skulking rail-like bird that is unlikely to be seen unless you’re expressly looking for it. The male is boldly red and black with white stripes, while the female is brownish and much plainer.
